metaTitle: Is Student Loan Forgiveness Taxable? 2026 Rules
metaDescription: Is student loan forgiveness taxable? Find out which discharges trigger federal income tax, how Section 108 exclusions work, and when insolvency applies.
h1: Is Student Loan Forgiveness Taxable? Federal Rules and Exclusions
cardBlurb: Federal tax on student loan forgiveness depends on the type of discharge and the year it is canceled, including whether it falls in the temporary 2021 to 2025 exclusion window.
introText:
Student loan forgiveness is taxable unless a specific federal exclusion covers the discharge. Under federal law, debt canceled by a creditor generally counts as gross income in the tax year the cancellation takes place. A temporary federal exclusion covered certain student loan discharges after December 31, 2020, and before January 1, 2026.

The test is whether the discharge falls under the professions provision, death or total and permanent disability, or the pre-2026 window. Borrowers who want to compare timelines can read our guide to [the student loan standard repayment plan](/guides/student-loan-standard-repayment-plan/).

sections.heading: When Forgiven Student Loans Are Taxable
sections.body:
Canceled student loan debt is taxable gross income unless an exclusion applies. Under [26 U.S.C. Section 61(a)(11)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/61), gross income includes income from the discharge of indebtedness. When a lender or program forgives an unpaid balance, that canceled obligation constitutes income for federal tax purposes.

According to [IRS Topic 431](https://www.irs.gov/taxtopics/tc431), nonbusiness canceled debt must be reported on Form 1040 or Form 1040-SR with Schedule 1 for the year in which the cancellation occurs. Work through three questions in order. Was the discharge made under a loan provision for working in certain professions? Was it due to the student's death or total and permanent disability? Did it occur after December 31, 2020, and before January 1, 2026? If the answer to all three is no, the canceled debt is generally income in the year it is canceled unless another exclusion, such as insolvency, applies.

For borrowers reaching the end of an income-driven repayment timeline, the discharged amount is generally taxable if no exclusion applies. This potential tax liability is called the student loan tax bomb. Borrowers who want to pay down a balance before any discharge can read our guide on [how to pay off debt](/guides/how-to-pay-off-debt/).

sections.heading: Which Discharges Are Excluded from Federal Gross Income
sections.body:
Federal law provides specific exclusions for student loan debt under [26 U.S.C. Section 108](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/108). Under Section 108(f)(1), gross income does not include a student loan discharge made under a loan provision that forgives debt if the borrower worked for a certain period of time in certain professions for any of a broad class of employers. Check whether your program is one that qualifies under Section 108(f)(1), using your loan documents, your servicer, or the IRS.

Discharges resulting from the death or total and permanent disability of the student are also excluded from federal income. Section 108(f)(5) excludes discharges after December 31, 2025, for federal student loans and private education loans due to death or total and permanent disability. To claim this exclusion on a federal tax return, the taxpayer must include their Social Security number on the return for that tax year.

IRS Topic 431 lists certain student loan discharges after December 31, 2020, and before January 1, 2026, as excluded from gross income. For discharges after December 31, 2025, the exclusions in this section are Section 108(f)(1) for qualifying professions and Section 108(f)(5) for death or total and permanent disability. Insolvency and bankruptcy exclusions are covered below.

sections.heading: Reporting Taxable Student Loan Debt
sections.body:
When a student loan discharge is taxable, the creditor or loan servicer may issue Form 1099-C showing the amount and date of cancellation. According to IRS Topic 431, you must report the correct taxable amount on your federal return regardless of whether the figures on Form 1099-C are accurate. If the form shows an incorrect amount or date, contact the creditor directly to request a corrected document.

Taxable discharge amounts are reported on Form 1040 or Form 1040-SR using Schedule 1. The canceled balance increases total gross income for the tax year of cancellation. Borrowers who want to restructure repayment before a balance reaches cancellation can compare options in [best student loan refinance companies](/roundup/best-student-loan-refinance/).

sections.heading: Reducing or Avoiding Tax Through the Insolvency Exclusion
sections.body:
Borrowers facing a taxable cancellation can reduce or eliminate the tax liability if they qualify as insolvent at the time of discharge. Under 26 U.S.C. Section 108(a)(1)(B), canceled debt is excluded from gross income if the discharge occurs when the taxpayer is insolvent. Section 108(d)(3) defines insolvency as the excess of liabilities over the fair market value of assets.

The insolvency exclusion is limited under Section 108(a)(3) to the dollar amount by which the taxpayer is insolvent. If total liabilities exceed total assets, up to that excess amount of canceled debt can be excluded from income. Any discharged amount beyond that insolvency calculation remains taxable gross income.

Debt canceled in a Title 11 bankruptcy case is also excluded from gross income under Section 108(a)(1)(A) and IRS Topic 431. Excluded amounts are reported on Form 982, Reduction of Tax Attributes Due to Discharge of Indebtedness, and generally require reducing tax attributes (IRS Topic 431).

sections.heading: State Tax Rules on Forgiven Student Debt
sections.body: State tax treatment of student loan forgiveness may differ from federal tax treatment. Check your state's rules.

sections.heading: Planning Steps for Potential Student Loan Discharges
sections.body:
Managing a student loan discharge requires tracking timelines, loan categories, and program criteria. Maintain copies of all promissory notes, loan agreements, and servicer communications regarding your repayment schedule. Verify whether your loan contains language tied to working in certain qualifying professions under Section 108(f)(1).

If a discharge may fall outside the temporary window and outside the professions and death or disability provisions, ask a tax professional or the IRS how it applies to you. Borrowers entering graduate study can read [how to pay for grad school](/guides/how-to-pay-for-grad-school/).

If your balance is canceled, check Form 1099-C for the cancellation date and amount, and contact the creditor if either is wrong. Next step: check whether your loan program qualifies under Section 108(f)(1), then confirm your situation with the IRS or your loan servicer.

faqs.question: Do I pay federal tax on forgiven student loans?
faqs.answer: It depends on the type of discharge and the date it occurs. Certain student loan discharges after December 31, 2020, and before January 1, 2026, were excluded from gross income under a temporary federal rule. Forgiveness that is not covered by that window, by the professions provision in Section 108(f)(1), or by death or total and permanent disability is generally included in income in the year it is canceled, unless another exclusion such as insolvency or bankruptcy applies.

faqs.question: Is forgiveness for working in certain professions taxable?
faqs.answer: Forgiveness for working in certain professions may be covered by Section 108(f)(1), which excludes from gross income a student loan discharge made under a loan provision that forgives debt if the borrower worked for a certain period of time in certain professions for any of a broad class of employers. Check whether your program is one that qualifies, and confirm with the IRS or your loan servicer.

faqs.question: What is the student loan tax bomb?
faqs.answer: The student loan tax bomb refers to the federal income tax owed when an unpaid student loan balance is canceled at the end of an income-driven repayment plan and is not covered by an exclusion. Because canceled debt is treated as gross income under Section 61(a)(11), the forgiven amount is added to the borrower's taxable income for that calendar year unless an exclusion applies.

faqs.question: Can I avoid tax on forgiven student loans if I am insolvent?
faqs.answer: Yes, under 26 U.S.C. Section 108(a)(1)(B), canceled debt is excluded from gross income if the taxpayer is insolvent when the discharge occurs. The exclusion is limited to the amount by which liabilities exceed the fair market value of assets under Section 108(a)(3), and is reported on Form 982.

faqs.question: Will I get a Form 1099-C for forgiven student loans?
faqs.answer: A creditor may issue Form 1099-C showing the canceled amount and date of discharge. IRS Topic 431 states that you must report the correct taxable amount on your return regardless of the form's accuracy, and you should contact the creditor if the form contains errors.
